programmes.d: Strawberry fills in at the bumblebee post office and learns that sometimes even when you try your very best, things don't always turn out as planned.
Strawberry struggles with how to be the berry best hostess when she has the very worst house guests.
Strawberry and her friends try to break a Berry Bitty World record to win a vacation for Berrykin Bloom.

Plum disregards Strawberry’s rule to sign up for use of the café, and is forced to reschedule a big dance recital. She holds a grudge and starts instigating wacky, nonsensical rules to prove rules are silly.
Berry Bitty City holds an election to see who will fill in as 'BerryFest Princess' while Princess Berrykin is absent.

When Strawberry finds herself in charge of the upcoming BerryFest parade, she hopes her gal pals can help her with the overwhelming amounts of chores. But each of them is rather demanding and ungracious, so they're no use at all.
As this year's BerryFest Princess, Strawberry must learn to be a leader, and overcome many obstacles, to make sure the festival is a success.

programmes.st: Nothing To Fear But Berries Themselves
programmes.d: When there's a blackout in Berry Bitty City, Orange discovers she has a fear of what's in the dark: a Galumphalot.

programmes.st: Where, Oh, Where Has Our Blueberry Gone?
programmes.d: Blueberry spends all her time emulating her literary detective hero and ignores her friends, until Strawberry gives her a 'missing person case' to solve—the missing person being Blueberry herself!
When the town’s very formal Berry Bitty Buggy Derby is revived, the girls are unfamiliar with the traditional behavior for the event.
Chaos ensues when Raspberry finds a way to enlarge the Berrykins to the same size as Strawberry and her friends.
Plum, determined to win a Dance-Off trophy, tries to get her friends and the Berrykins to dance just like a rival dance team, and learns that different people have different skills.
When Blueberry gives a First Frost Day 'secret' gift that's more what she wants than what her giftee wants, a hot-potato of passing on the unwanted gift occurs.
Raspberry is distraught when she suspects her friends have copied her design on her lantern for the 'Glimmerberry Gathering,' until she learns the true meaning behind the festival.
When the town needs a larger venue for their upcoming Glimmerberry Ball, Plum finds an ideal hollow tree for the occasion.
Lemon creates super-duper musical neon manicures, Glamicures. At first the other girls love them, then, because they are so bright and noisy, they begin to dislike them.

When a new game comes to Berry Bitty City, it starts to encroach on the other activities of the community. It falls to Orange to figure out how to give everyone in town their fair share of access to the public spaces.
When Sadiebug and Kadiebug create a new club, a 'Good Citizens Club,' Plum is suckered into doing their bidding, thinking that it's a 'test' for good citizenship.
Lemon and Raspberry have trouble collaborating on a decorating project, which causes all kinds of chaos... until they learn about teamwork.
Terribly worried when her beloved pets don't return home, Strawberry puts on a brave face so as not to worry her friends as they all search for the pets.
Orange's store is overflowing with Berrykin Bloom's new line of Berry Bitty Fruits & Veggies. Confident she can tackle any challenge, Orange tries to deal with everything herself.

Strawberry's new produce marketplace goes under construction. Strawberry is so grateful to her girlfriends for helping her with a new bedroom atop the marketplace, that she accommodates all their ideas and neglects to include her own!
Strawberry's friends surprise her by inviting her favorite singer, superstar Cherry Jam, to perform at the grand opening of the Marketplace.
When Cherry Jam plans a recital for her new music students, Plum experiences stage-fright for the first time, and tries to delay the event.

Berry Bitty City holds its first talent show. When the girls discover a talent scout will attend, Lemon decides she has to perform without any help from her friends, even though they are all helping each other.
Raspberry is discovered by a talent scout who wants her to move to Berry Big City and design a new line of Glitter fashions.
Blueberry overhears Strawberry talking about a wonderful tropical island and believes her friend is going to surprise them all with a much-needed vacation.
When the girls learn their tropical island vacation is cancelled due to weather, Orange decides to build an exact replica of the resort at home.
Just as the girls are about to enjoy a vacation at their homemade resort, TV host Mavis Maraschino shows up to do a segment on Cherry Jam and disrupts their plans.
The beginning of winter brings a brief spell of springlike weather, ruining everyone's hopes for winter fun. With help from Strawberry, the community adapts to the changing conditions.
Blueberry's invention of parasol-powered ice skates is all the rage, landing her the opportunity to create her own musical commercial for them.

When both Raspberry and Berrykin Bruce plan spring-themed events for the same location, Strawberry helps them work out a compromise—they combine their efforts to create a spring fashion show around a water show.

The girls' new band is about to go on the road to a concert at Berry Big City. But first they must teach the Berrykins all about their businesses, so the little folk can keep the community running until the girls return.
On his way to Berry Big City to open a home for stray dogs, Huckleberry Pie’s Pet-Mobile gets stuck. He is rescued by Strawberry and her friends.
Blueberry entices Huckleberry to come for a visit by asking him to team up and write a mystery story for an online mystery magazine.

When Shredder schemes to create a fearsome army of mutants, the Turtles have no choice but to rely on the help of the newest recruit to the Foot Clan: The Pulverizer!

Morticia and Gomez visit Mayor Henson to complain that their property tax is ridiculously low. After the Mayor proves his incompetence by offering a refund, Gomez is persuaded to become a candidate for the office.

Dr. Marvin P. Gunderson is summoned to examine Kitty Kat, the ailing lion pet of the Addams Family. Morticia decides that it is the doctor who needs help. To build his confidence, human members of the family pretend to be ill so he can effect cures.

Because she thinks Fester (Jackie Coogan) and Grandmama (Blossom Rock) are spoiling the children, Morticia (Carolyn Jones) hires a governess. Insulted, Fester paints a white line down the center of the Addams house, dividing it in half.

Uncle Fester's pen pal, Madelyn, is coming to visit. Fester panics, as he has described himself as handsome, heroic and romantic.  Gomez and Morticia agree that all Fester needs is a toupee and they help him make several styles.

Morticia calls a psychiatrist after she fears Pugsley is becoming normal after he abandons his pet octopus for a puppy and is seen wearing a Boy Scout uniform, playing with a baseball bat, and helping an old lady cross the street.

When Wednesday's and Pugsley's faith in Santa Claus is shaken, Uncle Fester is chosen to back up Santa in case the real St. Nick is too busy to come. However, Fester-Santa gets stuck in the chimney, so each of the other adults fills in for him.

The family would like to vacation on the moon, but the billion-dollar travel cost is slightly prohibitive. Uncle Fester volunteers $21.13 and Morticia, using Gomez's new supercomputer, suggests placing a $2,000 bet on the daily double horse race.

Thing disappears from his box. Failing to find a single trace of Thing, Gomez (John Astin) conducts an investigation--with all members of the household under suspicion. Also starring Carolyn Jones, Jackie Coogan, and Ted Cassidy.

During a welcome home party for Cousin Itt, Morticia notices that the diminutive guest of honor seems to be losing his hair. Uncle Fester experiments with his chemistry set to produce a concoction that grows hair and tries the remedy on Itt.

The family faces a crisis when Wednesday packs her spider and runs away (after being scolded for playing with Uncle Fester's TNT). When they try to file a missing person report, a detective is anxious to retire early due to their story.

Lurch becomes a veritable gazelle when he takes dancing lessons at Gomez and Morticia's suggestion after he admits to being a wallflower at social functions.  Each member of the Addams Family teaches Lurch a different step.

A pair of bank robbers are welcomed as Halloween trick-or-treaters by Morticia and Gomez.  The creepy atmosphere of the house, Morticia's smoldering holiday punch, and Lurch's ominous presence impel the crooks to abandon their plans.

programmes.st: Addams Family Meets The Undercover Man
programmes.d: Mr. Briggs, the postman, is hired by the government to do undercover work in the Addams house.  While pretending to be a stamp collector, he investigates rumors that coded radio messages are being sent from the house.

programmes.st: The Addams Family Meets A Beatnik
programmes.d: Rockland Cartright III is a beatnik who crashes his motorbike into a tree and recuperates at the Addams house.  Each regards the other as an oddity, although the family learns to appreciate certain aspects of Rockland's life.

Fester is so smitten upon receipt of a photo of his love, a bearded carnival lady, that he borrows stamp money to mail her a proposal. Morticia dons a beard and poses as the mother to convince Fester that he will have to work to support a wife.

Gomez (John Astin) loses his memory after hitting his head; he fails to recognize Morticia (Carolyn Jones) and says the house looks like a condemned museum.  The Addamses take turns hitting Gomez on the head trying to help him regain his memory.

After Pugsley befriends Gorgo, a circus gorilla, Gorgo decides to follow Pugsley and Gomez home, where is accepted as one of the family. But Gorgo gives Morticia's tea guests, the Ladies League members, quite a shock.

programmes.st: Mother Lurch Visits The Addams Family
programmes.d: Lurch's tiny fire-eating mother visits and demands that Lurch's employers wait on her boy hand-and-foot after Lurch leads her to believe that it's his house. Lurch revels in the unexpected attention he gets from Morticia and Gomez.

programmes.st: The Addams Family Meets The V.I.P.'s
programmes.d: Official visitors from an unfriendly nation receive the shock of their lives when they decide to exploit the Addams Family as an average uncultured family. The visitors are shaken up by Morticia's carnivorous plants among other things.

Morticia's cousin, Melancholia, wants to marry Clarence P. Harvey after most of her marital prospects have joined the Foreign Legion. Clarence recoils when Melancholia puts on a campaign to win him, backed by Morticia, Gomez and Clarence's boss.

Grandmama (Blossom Rock) is hauled off to jail for setting up a fortune-telling booth in the Addamses' living room.  Gomez (John Astin) volunteers to act as attorney, and the court session becomes a shambles.

Ophelia taunts Uncle Fester into announcing that he is going to join the Peace Corps. Fester feels he's a cinch to be accepted because Gomez plans to pull strings in Washington on his behalf. The entire family agrees to help him study for the exam.

An organ grinder's fugitive monkey leads Fester to believe that he has turned Pugsley into a monkey.  Morticia and Gomez treat the monkey as though he were their son, welcoming him to the dinner table and giving him Pugsley's chores.

Gomez plays host to Don Xavier Molines, a family friend during his childhood in Spain, and his daughter Consuella.  Morticia's hospitality is put to the test when Consuella reveals that she has been promised in marriage to Gomez since childhood.

Lurch suffers from unrequited love over Tiny Trivia (guest star Diane Jergens), Morticia's visiting school chum who only has eyes for show business.  The entire family decides to try to turn their stolid butler into a new personality.

Pugsley and Wednesday start a row at a party when their gift of a tarantula upsets Harold, the birthday boy.  Harold's parents insist that the Addams children lack breeding and, therefore, are no longer allowed to play with their son.

Morticia, in order to be part of the National Beautification Program, decides to become a home decorator and offers her services to the neighbors. Next door neighbor, and insurance agent, Joe Digby hires Morticia in hopes of selling them insurance.

Ophelia Frump is madly in love with Horatio Bartholomew, the man who has everything, except the truth about her relatives. Morticia, not convinced by Bartholomew, persuades playboy Cousin Itt to stir the embers of his past romance with Ophelia.

There is a neighborhood burglar on the loose, and Morticia has reason to believe it could be Gomez.  Morticia decides to probe his subconscious mind for a key to his criminality after she and Uncle Fester discover loot hidden in the storeroom.

programmes.st: The Addams Family Meets A Beatnik
programmes.d: Rockland Cartright III is a beatnik who crashes his motorbike into a tree and recuperates at the Addams house.  Each regards the other as an oddity, although the family learns to appreciate certain aspects of Rockland's life.

After Wednesday befriends a new boy her age, Robespierre Courtney, Morticia invites his parents, Mr. and Mrs. Henry Courtney to visit the Addams house for tea. Unbeknownst to them, the Courtney's are hoping to meet a number of the social set.

programmes.st: Cousin Itt Visits The Addams Family
programmes.d: Cousin Itt is advocated as curator of the local zoo.  Gomez uses his influence with Park Commissioner Fisk (guest star Alan Reed) to promote Itt for the job, but the zookeepers are convinced the Addamses' cousin should be confined to a cage.

Allyn Joslyn guest-stars as Sam Hilliard, a former truant officer who now heads a private school where Wednesday and Pugsley are enrolled. When Hilliard breaks under the strain of dealing with the Addams children, Gomez buys the school.
A Hollywood producer descends on Mayberry and the town proceeds to make itself over in Hollywood's image.
Barney starts wearing his uniform all the time after being threatened with bodily harm if he's ever caught without it on.
Barney interprets a kiss as a sign of a secret engagement between Andy and Helen. The town gets the word and prepares a surprise party for the couple.
Opie accidentally kills a bird with a slingshot and becomes foster-mother to her three young birds.
Opie and his chums take their roles as Robin Hood and his merry men seriously as they befriend a hobo at the expense of the pantries of Mayberry.
Andy tries to counsel the constantly bickering couple, Fred and Jennie Boone, with mixed results.
Aunt Bee is the unwilling object of matrimony when mountaineer Briscoe Darling comes a'courting.
Andy and Opie struggle to keep house when Aunt Bee leaves for a few days.

programmes.st: The Education of Ernest T. Bass

Goober dismantles a car in the sheriff's office.
Barney Fife buys a bloodhound to aid in Mayberry law enforcement.

A hometown guitar player auditions with a dance band in the Mayberry jail.
Andy goes to Raleigh for a job interview and chaos prevails in Mayberry with Barney Fife as acting sheriff.
Andy, appointed judge of a beauty contest, shows the wisdom of Solomon by picking a popular winner.
Opie becomes jealous when his father appears to be paying special attention to a pretty girl -- even taking her fishing with them.
Andy and Ellie give the Cinderella treatment to a farmer's daughter.
A nationally known con man becomes a hero to Aunt Bee, Opie and Barney when he is held for two days in the Mayberry jail.
Andy uses common sense and Barney uses modern criminal detection methods to solve several burglaries at a filling station.
Barney Fife decides to dabble in real estate as a side job. He tries to get the sheriff to put his house up for sale.
Howard Morris guest stars as Ernest T. Bass as the Darling clan returns to Mayberry with its own kind of mountain trouble.
The Mayberry mayor demands that Andy get a crime expert from the city to help solve several cow thefts.
Andy tries to stop a long-time feud between 2 mountain families so their children can get married.
The sheriff has his hands full as a clan of mountain musicians descend on Mayberry to meet a bus.
Opie must either learn how to box or lose prestige among his peers when a new boy moves into town.
Andy, faced with the unpleasant duty of serving an eviction notice, discovers a way to save the mortgagee's home.
Andy suspects that a traveling record promoter is a con artist and he fears for the townsfolk who invested in his record.
Andy and Barney give a Christmas party in the jail for a prisoner and his family, and thereby convert the town scrooge.
Barney Fife is convinced that Opie's piggy bank is safer than the Mayberry bank-and sets out to prove his point.

Lucas's old Army pal settles in North Fork with his deaf daughter.
An Englishman arrives with a custom-made rifle and a plan to kill Lucas.
Mark falls head-over-heels in puppy love.
Banker Hamilton is closing up for the day when Rudy Gray persuades him to stay open for one more transaction...a withdrawal at gunpoint.
Tip Corey, the son of a man allegedly murdered in North Fork, has a killer's reputation and comes to town to kill Micah.
Len Richards and his brother, Ab, confront a Lucas McCain look-alike, Earl Bantry and his sidekick K.C. Peters, for slaughtering one of Richards' steers.
Lucas and Mark stop on the way to the county fair to deliver a message to Micah, who is escorting a prisoner to be hanged. Mark and Lucas recognize the prisoner.
Mark and Milly are shocked when Lucas begins gambling. They don't know that Lucas is "undercover" trying to catch a man cheating.
Mark befriends singer-banjoist Lafayette Bly, a blind man with an acute sense of hearing and a very strong grip.
A retired lawman's irrational jealousy threatens not only to destroy his marriage but also to make him an easy target for someone who wants him dead.
No one is more surprised than Micah when newcomer Leota Carraway claims he's her long-lost husband and the father of her child.
Lucas is torn by conflicting emotions when he meets the town's new preacher, a former outlaw whom the Rifleman vowed to kill.
The town of North Fork becomes a haven for outlaws when suave Ben Judson smooth-talks his way into the marshal's job.
A handsome gambler moves into town and begins wooing Milly Scott, claiming to have known her deceased brother.
Lucas develops temporary amnesia from a head injury while visiting a strange town and mistakenly assumes the identity of a wanted criminal.
A former neighbor of the McCains' is released from jail after serving his sentence for robbery. Lucas lets the man work for him but the new hand holds a secret.
When Lucas, Mark, and Micah get lost in Old Mexico, they are held hostage by a group of bandits who intend to kill the men and take Mark as a slave.
While trapped in the ghost town saloon, Lucas tries to come up with a plan to escape with his son and Micah after Mark refuses to leave without him.
Lou Mallory arrives in North Fork and starts buying up land and businesses. Lou and Lucas start disliking each other after she reveals plans to build a railroad on "worthless" land.
When a woman arrives in North Fork with symptoms of smallpox, Lucas, Lou Mallory, Doctor Burrage, and hotel occupants are quarantined in the hotel with an outlaw.
Gunslinger Johnny Drako rides into town and tells the bartender that he is looking for Lucas McCain. After Johnny leaves the saloon, Sweeney hurries to tell Lucas.
A man arrives in North Fork, intending to marry Lou Mallory. The hotel owner looks for a way out from marrying the man to whom her dying father promised her.
An assassination plot unfolds as four gunmen disguised as cavalrymen enter North Fork. Their target: Sen. Jim Borden. Their weapon: a Gatling gun.
Sharpshooter Marty Blair tries to persuade Lucas to buy Mark a rifle. After Lucas shoots a man during a robbery at the hotel, Mark and Lucas disagree with his character.
Fast-draw artist Wade Randall is in town, bragging of his gun battles with notorious bad men until one of them shows up to challenge his story.
When Lucas refuses to sell his land, Mr. Prescott will stop at nothing to  change his mind. He hires men to try to persuade Lucas, but he refuses.
Mark's careless actions cause the death of a friend. Unable to accept the truth, he blames the rifle and runs away from home. Soon, he is faced with a tough decision.
Nils Swenson takes the marshal's place for a few days while Micah is away. To maintain peace, Nils insists that anyone coming into town must turn in their weapons.
Lucas's self-confidence begins to slip away when he misses an easy shot that could have cost Mark his life.
A murder occurs at a railroad camp and a young Indian friend of Lucas is accused of the killing. When Lucas tries to help the boy, he finds himself on trial.
Lucas and Mark come upon Winslow Quince, a peddler whose wagon has broken down. They help him bring his wagon to North Fork for repair.
Gridley Mau, the son of a man Lucas killed during an attempted robbery, comes to North Fork looking for revenge.
The first railroad train is coming to the new North Fork station. Onboard is a Japanese nobleman and his servant, visiting the West to learn about the United States.
Barbara accidentally causes her cruel Uncle Simon's death. His will stipulates that she must care for his latest invention - a robot. The robot begins to take on Uncle Simon's traits.
A timid vacuum-cleaner salesman is given the strength of 300 men by some experimenting aliens.
Walter Jameson is an excellent history teacher who talks about the past as if he had lived it.
Jared Garrity arrives in the Old West town of Happiness, Arizona, proclaiming he can revive the dead.

An elderly private school teacher wonders if his life has meant anything as he contemplates suicide on Christmas Eve and is reminded by former students that he has, indeed, had an impact on their lives.
Using the power of mind over matter, Archibald Beechcroft remakes the world to his own specifications.

A US naval destroyer investigates a mysterious tapping sound coming from a sunken submarine.
A singer's song becomes tragically real.
When three dum-dum crooks get ahold of a camera that takes pictures of the future, they set out to make a quick fortune with their new toy.
A man is terrified of falling asleep for fear he might die.
A young couple book passage on a trans-Atlantic cruise, hoping to salvage their marriage.
On a hunting trip, Hyder Simpson and his dog Rip dive into a lake after a raccoon. When he gets home he finds that no one can see or hear him.
A has-been, drunk gunslinger finds his fast-draw abilities magically restored.
An old man fears that he will die if his grandfather clock stops running.

Major Ivan Kuchenko is trapped inside a hotel room with Commissar Vassiloff, a hitman, and Boris, his assistant, in the room across the street. Vassiloff has planted a bomb in the room and Ivan must find it within three hours or be blown to bits.
The senior residents of Sunnyvale decide that the secret to youth is acting young, and in particular playing a childhood game called "kick-the-can."

programmes.st: Nervous Man in a Four Dollar Room
programmes.d: Small time criminal Jackie Rhoades must face both his past and his conscience while waiting for his next assignment.
A street salesman cleverly eludes Death. But if he lives, a little girl must die in his place.
A computer technician must deal with the queen of all femme fatales: a computer named Agnes who wreaks havoc on his love life.
A dying man demands his family wear masks that he's given them at a Mardi Gras party.
When a woman investigates a clamor on the roof of her rural house, she discovers a small UFO and little aliens emerging from it. Or so it seems.
The lone survivors of two annihilated worlds are stranded on a distant planet.
A young woman lying in a hospital bed, her head wrapped in bandages, awaits the outcome of a surgical procedure performed by the State in a last-ditch attempt to make her look 'normal'.
With all-out nuclear war about to ignite, a scientist and his pilot friend plot to escape on an experimental spaceship.
Lt. Fitzgerald has found his own special wartime hell. Looking into the faces of his men prior to battle, he has the disquieting ability to see who is about to die.
Erich is displeased when his wife buys an expensive doll for his step-daughter. He becomes even more displeased when the doll tells him it doesn't like him!
The Kanamits, 9-foot tall aliens, arrive on Earth with one lofty goal: To Serve Man.
Old Ben, who is able to transform himself into anything, tries to help a crippled little girl.
When a newlywed couple briefly returns to the groom's childhood home, the ties of the past prove too strong to resist.

Agents West and Gordon again face Dr. Loveless whom, planning to rule a world of "little people," reduces West to a six-inch miniature.

programmes.d: Agents West and Gordon visit a town named Justice during Law and Order Seek and find it the site for a convention of criminals.

programmes.d: Secret agents James T. West and Artemus Gordon are assigned to free a fellow agent from Devil's Island.

programmes.d: Secret agent West is kidnapped by a madman who plans to create an underwater kingdom that will control the world's shipping lanes.

programmes.d: The evil, diminutive Dr. Loveless impoverishes an Indian tribe so that he can become their benefactor -- and their god.

Jack finds himself in hot water when best friends Larry's girl says she still has a mad crush on him.

Terri falls for Jack when he buys a mustache which makes him look like her old boyfriend.
Jack snows a stunning skier named Inga into believing he's a downhill champion.
Janet moves in with Mrs. Roper while Mr. Roper is away on business, then stews about Jack and Chrissy being alone for the night in the trio's upstairs apartment.
Jack, Janet, and Chrissy face having to split up when Chrissy's father, Reverend Snow, announces that their special living arrangement jeopardizes his appointment as the new local minister.
The women in Jack's life go to a nude beach protest and run into trouble with the cops.
Ralph Furley tries to impress his childhood rival by introducing Chrissy as his new bride.
To boost Jack's confidence, Terri turns on the charm, causing Janet to suspect that her new roommate's interest in Jack is more than platonic.
Jack is conned into renting a small restaurant - only to discover that it's a run-down disaster. Guest Star(s): Jordan Charney

Janet and Chrissy think it's great when they learn that Jack is dating a "fantastic" older woman.
A tiny tyke terrorizes Jack and Chrissy with the threat of tears after Janet presses them into service as inexperienced, substitute sitters.
When an absent-minded policeman leaves his handcuffs at the trio's apartment, Chrissy and Jack playfully slap the cuffs on each other and then discover there's no key. Guest Star(s): Heather Lowe

programmes.t: Sugar Ray Leonard vs Marvin Hagler
programmes.d: On April 6th, 1987 Sugar Ray Leonard fought Marvin Hagler for the WBC World Middleweight title at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas in a twelve round bout that resulted in a split decision in favor of Leonard.

programmes.t: Sugar Ray Leonard vs Thomas Hearns
programmes.d: On September 16th, 1981 Sugar Ray Leonard faced Thomas Hearns for the WBA and WBC World welterweight titles at the Caesars Palace in Las Vegas resulting in a win by technical knockout for Leonard and went on to be the 1981 Fight of the year.

programmes.t: Sugar Ray Leonard vs Wilfred Benitez
programmes.d: On November 30th, 1979 Sugar Ray Leonard fought Wilfred Benitez for the WBC World Welterweight title at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas that went 15 rounds but ended in technical knockout giving the victory to Leonard.

On August 13th, 2022, Teofimo Lopez fought Pedro Campa for the NABF & WBO International Super Lightweight Titles in Las Vegas. Teofimo looked confident and quick from the start, wearing down Campa until he finally stopped him in the 7th round.

On October 17th, 2020 Teofimo Lopez and Vasiliy Lomachenko battled for IBF, WBA and WBO World Lightweight title in The Bubble at MGM Grand in Las Vegas in a 12 round bout that ended in victory for Lopez.

On July 14th, 2018 Teofimo Lopez and William Silva fought for the vacant WBC Continental Americas lightweight titles with Silva going down 3 times Lopez secured the technical knockout win in the sixth round.
On April 14th, 2012 Terence Crawford fought Andre Gorges at the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas in a bout that was set for 6 round and lasted 5 with a win by knockout victory for Crawford.

programmes.t: Terence Crawford vs Jose Benavidez Jr
programmes.d: On October 13th, 2018, Terence Crawford fought Jose Benavidez Jr for the WBO World Welterweight Title in Omaha, Nebraska. In a dominant performance, Crawford showed out in front of his hometown, delivering a TKO in the final round.

On August 19th, 2017 Terence Crawford fought Julius Indongo for the IBF, WBA, WBC and WBO  World Super Lightweight titles at the Pinnacle Bank Arena in Lincoln the bout ended in the third round by knockout securing the victory for Crawford.

On November 14th, 2020 Terence Crawford battled Kell Brook for the WBO World Welterweight title in The Bubble at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas resulting in a fourth round technical knockout victory for Crawford.

On November 20th, 2021, Terence Crawford fought Shawn Porter for the WBO World Welterweight Title at the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. In a very close fight, Crawford turned it up and put on the pressure late, delivering a TKO in the 10th round.

On April 18th, 2015, Terence Crawford fought Thomas Dulorme for the WBO World Super Lightweight Title in Arlington, Texas. Putting on the pressure and showing his aggressive style, Crawford scored three knockdowns in the sixth round to get the TKO.

On July 23rd, 2016, Terence Crawford fought Viktor Postol for the WBO and WBC World Super Lightweight Titles at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Scoring two knockdowns, Crawford dominated the fight, earning a much deserved unanimous decision victory.

On June 28th, 2014, Terence Crawford fought Yuriorkis Gamboa for the WBO Lightweight Title at Century Link Center in Omaha. In Top Rank's 2014 Fight of the Year, Terence Crawford shined in front of his hometown, stopping Gamboa in the ninth round.

programmes.t: Thomas Hearns vs Juan Domingo Roldan
programmes.d: On October 29th, 1987 Thomas Hearns faced Juan Domingo Roldan for the vacant WBC World Middleweight title at the Las Vegas Hilton the 12 round bout went only 4 rounds ending with a knockout by Hearns securing the victory.

On June 15th, 1984 Thomas Hearns fought Roberto Duran for WBC World Super Welterweight title at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas that resulted in a technical knockout victory in the second round by Hearns.

programmes.t: Timothy Bradley Jr vs Kendall Holt
programmes.d: On April 4th, 2009, Timothy Bradley Jr fought Kendall Holt for the WBC and WBO Light Welterweight Titles at the Bell Centre in Montreal. Holt scored two knockdowns to keep the fight close, but Bradley stayed aggressive enough to earn the decision.

programmes.t: Timothy Bradley Jr vs Ruslan Provodnikov
programmes.d: On March 16th, 2013, Timothy Bradley fought Ruslan Provodnikov for the WBO Welterweight Title in Carson, California. Provodnikov put up a very strong challenge in an incredible fight, but Bradley prevailed, earning a unanimous decision victory.

programmes.t: Timothy Bradley vs Manny Pacquiao I
programmes.d: On June 9th, 2012 Manny Pacquiao and Timothy Bradley started their trilogy at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas in a battle for the WBO World Welterweight title that ended in a split decision win for Timothy Bradley.
On August 6th, 1992 Todd Foster fought Jeff Mayweather at Denton Field in Miles City with Mayweather going down in rounds 7 & 8 the bout resulted in a technical knockout victory for Foster.

On June 7th, 1993 Tommy Morrison battled George Foreman for the WBO world heavyweight title at the Thomas & Mack Center in Las Vegas with Foreman getting a point deducted in round ten the bout resulted in a victory for Morrison.

Since the dawn of civilization, humanity has been fixated on predicting our own demise.

All over the world, there are places and objects that are thought to be cursed; many people avoid these locations and things, believing they will bring harm, while others think that curses are nothing more than superstition and folklore.
For centuries, fantastic tales of terrifying monsters have fascinated mankind; bizarre beasts of all shapes and sizes have been portrayed in some of history's most classic stories and folklore.
A look at the visions of mystics, prophets and clairvoyants throughout history, what their prophecies reveal and predictions for the future.
Scientists are involved in a never-ending quest to understand the vast universe the planet inhabits; it seems that for each answer science provides, even more questions arise.

More than 7 billion people live on Earth; human civilizations span the globe; although many around the globe believe that the divine hand of God placed humans on Earth, others question whether there were ever other kinds of human-like creatures.

Whether surviving freezing temperatures, diving unfathomable depths in one breath, or lifting weighty objects, superhuman feats never cease to amaze; pulling them off could be a matter of training, willpower, genetics, or something more mysterious.

Hollister captures outlaw Lafe Jackson who is on his way to a rendezvous with his gang to divide the proceeds of a robbery. Lafe kills both horses, forcing Clay to take his prisoner in on foot, giving Lafe's gang time to catch up and rescue him.

Hollister doesn't know the identity of the 'brain' directing an epidemic of outlawry in the Territory. But when handsome Horn Burnett and his brother commit murder, the attachment of a rancher's wife for the outlaw gives Clay a hint at the truth.

An annual family holiday tradition quickly turned into a deadly nightmare. And now the man accused of ramming an SUV into a Christmas parade was standing trial and facing some of those who were there.

Prosecutors kept bringing in witnesses who had been at the parade when an SUV came crashing into the crowd. The State's latest witness was a woman who had been hit, along with her 9-year-old daughter.
A survivor is cross-examined by the same man accused of hitting her and her daughter with his car.
Traumatized and grieving survivors, including two youth baseball coaches, take the witness stand.

A dance team coach took the stand in the deadly parade crash trial and gave a harrowing account of how a red SUV hit many of the dancers in her group. They were among the sixty-one people injured. In the end, six people died.
A dance coach breaks down remembering the moment she and her team faced the oncoming car.
The State's main focus at this point in the deadly parade crash trial was on calling the survivors to the stand. In all, six people died when an SUV plowed into the crowd.

Investigators looked into every part of the building where Botham was killed.

(1/4) The TARDIS is drawn into an empty void, but they are not the only ones trapped there.
(2/4) When Rorvik learns that Romana is a time sensitive, he takes her prisoner.
(3/4) As the void shrinks, Rorvik plans to take desperate measures to escape via the mirror.
(4/4) Rorvik ignores the Doctor's warnings and takes a gamble which may have fatal consequences.
(1/4) The Keeper of Traken appears in the TARDIS seeking the Doctor's help.
(2/4) The Traken Consul hold Adric and the Doctor under sentence of death.
(3/4) Kassia, now the willing servant of the Melkur, is to become the new Keeper of Traken.
(4/4) Kassia completes the transition. The Melkur is only a shell, the real power lies within.
(1/4) To repair the TARDIS's chameleon circuit, the Doctor goes to Earth for a real police box.
(2/4) The Doctor travels to Logopolis where a series of fateful events are set in motion.
(3/4) The Master is loose on Logopolis and is determined to learn the planet's secret.
(4/4) With the fate of the universe at stake, the Doctor and the Master must collaborate.
(1/4) The arrival of the TARDIS is observed by three Urbankans.
(2/4) A Grecian philosopher reveals a bizarre secret about Monarch.
(3/4) Tegan accidentally pilots the TARDS into space, while Lin Fitu betrays the Doctor.
(4/4) The Doctor undertakes a dangerous spacewalk to rescue Tegan.
(1/4) 17th century England is being stalked by a robotic death-like figure.
(2/4) The Terileptil leader is planning to wipe out mankind with plague rats.
(3/4) A mesmerized Tegan prepares to unleash the rats on the Doctor and Richard Mace.
(4/4) Heading to London Town, the Doctor discovers more Terileptil criminals in hiding.
(1/4) On Deva Loka, Tegan falls asleep in the forest watched by the Kinda.
(2/4) When Hindle's breakdown begins, the Doctor and Todd are in danger.
(3/4) Panna shows the Doctor what the past, present and future holds for Deva Loka.
(4/4) The Mara finally breaks free of its dream dimension.
(1/4) The Doctor tries to recuperate within the Zero Room.
(2/4) The Zero Room is gone, and the Doctors regeneration is unstable.
(3/4) Something is wrong with Castrovalva, but the Portreeve cannot help.
(4/4) A recursive occlusion threatens to destroy everything and everyone in Castrovalva.
(1/2) As UNIT are transporting a nuclear warhead around Carbury, knights in armour arrive.
(2/2) The Doctor and Ace explore King Arthurs spaceship deep under Lake Vortigern.
(1/4) Silent but deadly androids are protecting a bomb buried beneath the Earth.
(2/4) With her crew slowly vanishing, Briggs assumes the Doctor to be the guilty party.
(3/4) The Cybermen are released from their silos and on the march.
(4/4) The Doctor realizes the freighter is now a huge bomb, with one passenger still aboard.
Concorde disappears back through a crack in time, so the Doctor follows its trail.
After an encounter with the Plasmatons, Nyssa is possessed by strange aliens.
From within their sarcophagus, the gestalt Xeraphin are communicating through Nyssa.
The Master's TARDIS repaired, the Doctor must follow him back to 20th century Heathrow.
The Doctor and Nyssa trace something odd to Amsterdam...
Commander Maxil doesn't believe the Doctor is innocent.
Within the Matrix, the Doctor unmasks Omega and realizes the threat is far from over...
Omega has been reborn but as a walking anti-matter bomb.
(1/4) Caught in a warp ellipse, the TARDIS is drawn to a huge spacecraft.
(2/4) At Brendon School, the Doctor enlists the help of the Brigadier.
(3/4) Mawdryn and his eternal mutants are awake and reveal the truth.
(4/4) The Doctors ethics are challenged and the two Brigadier's finally meet.
Turlough sabotages the TARDIS causing it to fuse with the space station Terminus.
Bor solves the mystery at the heart of Terminus itself.
The Doctor finds the pilot of Terminus and realises a mistake is about to be made.
The Garm and the pirates stop Terminus setting off a second Big Bang.
The Doctor receives a dire warning from the White Guardian.
The Doctor realizes that Striker is an Eternal and that the crew mean nothing to him.
During an Eternals party, Captain Wrack places a bomb aboard Striker's ship.
Turlough must make a decision and the Doctor and Tegan are unable to help him.

programmes.d: (1/2) At a medieval joust, the TARDIS appears.

programmes.t: Classic Doctor Who: The King's Demons
programmes.d: (2/2) The Master and the Doctor fight for control over Kamelions mind.
(1/4) Seabase 4 is on alert as a strange craft approaches.
(2/4) The Silurians and Sea Devils send the Myrka in as a spearhead to an invasion.
(3/4) Vorshak's crew are cut down one by one by Sauvix's Sea Devil Warriors.
(4/4) The Doctor is despondent that no one wants to find another way to avoid so much death.

Monty Don travels to some of the most celebrated artists' gardens, including the one created by the impressionist Claude Monet, who planted and painted his garden for half his life. Monty also matches the paintings to the garden of Paul Cezanne, as well as visiting several contemporary artistic gardens to see how the use of plants and trees has evolved into new and varied styles.

Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

Monty begins in the city of Trieste, close to Italy's border with Croatia, to visit a public garden first created by an obsessive royal plantsman more than 150 years ago, which is now being carefully restored. He then heads down the Adriatic coast through Croatia to pick up the trail that the Venetians followed, ending his journey on the beautiful island of Lopud, near Dubrovnik.

Monty travels to Europe and explores the influence of the Venetians on gardening. To begin with, he explores Venice on one of the city's famous barges, stepping out to visit green spaces large and small that are often hidden from view behind high walls.

Monty begins the last leg of his journey in Corfu, a Greek island with strong Venetian links, including olive trees planted by them that are still grown today. Here, Monty visits a spectacular garden made by an Englishman with Greek connections.

Monty propagates succulent plants, revisits his container vegetable garden, and gives advice on how to get a good crop of pumpkins. Adam looks a new garden at RHS Hyde Hall in Essex, and Rachel visits a garden of vibrant colours in Wiltshire.

Adam Frost is in his garden, bringing viewers up to date on how it has been developing, as well as giving advice on growing hydrangeas. Toby Buckland shares his tips on dealing with damaged shrubs, tree pruning and transplanting perennials.

Monty refreshes a container of overgrown herbs, plants alpines and revisits the shrub and perennial cuttings he took a few weeks ago. Arit Anderson meets a designer who is placing sustainability and the environment at the heart of her gardens.

One couple battle to turn a clay-clogged building site in Sussex into a piece of Portugal. Another tackle a forest of overgrowth in their new back garden in Cadeby. They are determined to create a productive space, something they have always wanted.

A truck driver from Wakefield with a passion for flowers wants to create a perfect outside space for his girlfriend and burgeoning family, while in Swindon a widow wants to find the best way of turning her bleak patch of green into a cottage garden.

programmes.t: The Secret History of the British Garden
programmes.d: Starting his journey at the sole surviving garden of the 1600s, Levens Hall in Cumbria, Monty sets out to investigate what the gardens of this age would have looked like and what influenced and inspired their creation.

programmes.t: The Secret History of the British Garden
programmes.d: Monty bases himself at Rousham House in Oxfordshire, designed by one of the first practitioners of the landscape movement, William Kent. It has survived almost unchanged since its completion in 1741.

programmes.t: The Secret History of the British Garden
programmes.d: Monty Don explores the extraordinary transformations that occurred throughout the 19th century. As a result of an expanding empire, scientific and technological innovation and social change, British gardens became more exotic, more colourful and more widely accessible than ever before.

programmes.t: The Secret History of the British Garden
programmes.d: Monty Don concludes his journey through Britain's gardening heritage by looking at how the nation's gardens have evolved over the last hundred years. He looks at the profound effect that two world wars had on the attitude to gardens and gardening.

As the borders at Longmeadow hit their stride, it's time to take stock of what's looking good and what needs replacing. Monty shares his tips on how to keep the display going all summer long. There's plenty to do on the vegetable plot too and things are looking promising in the fruit garden.

Monty catches up with maintaining his pond and gives advice on planting water lilies. He also gives tips on how to grow and plant herbaceous clematis as well as harvesting potatoes. Nick Bailey begins his guide to demystifying roses, Arit Anderson takes a trip on a canal boat to find out how volunteers are bringing plants and wildlife back into the city of Birmingham, Mark Lane gives his guide on how to get the cottage style look into the garden.

Whether there is a heatwave or a downpour, Monty has plenty of jobs to be getting on with from pruning, propagating or planting pots. Adam Frost meets Prince Charles in his garden at Highgrove to talk about the issue of biosecurity, an issue which is of great concern to him and which could have a big effect on our gardens and landscape. Adam also talks to The Prince's Head Forester to find out what gardeners can do to help.

Monty advises on plants for a late summer display, tackles his overgrown wildlife pond and shows which roses to prune now for a repeat flowering in late summer. Frances Tophill travels to Birmingham where she shows that every space counts by transforming three tiny balconies into spaces full of colour and scent.

In Southampton, sociable bachelor Morgan has £5,000 for a party garden, with a nod to his years at sea working on cruise ships. The space must also have privacy, a water feature and, as a proud Welshman, the feeling of his homeland.

The Rich brothers are joined by Arit Anderson to help create an all-year-round garden in Byfleet for stylish octogenarian Gay, to enjoy the birds and remember her late husband. She wants a garden which is simple to manage, but also welcoming.

The team are in Shoreham by Sea, helping John and David. They have £4,500 to turn their tired garden into the perfect place to host their wedding reception. With a relatively small house, the surprisingly spacious outside space must pull its weight.

Karen and Duncan in Shefford complain that their garden is too plain, and they don't like straight lines so they want curves instead. The Rich brothers and Arit Anderson try to create something modern but which also has rustic elements.

Monty travels from Missouri to Chicago and then across to New York and Philadelphia. He begins his journey in a prairie, the original American flowering wilderness. Much of the prairie has disappeared but he meets a couple who have revived the tradition and enjoy showing it to him in full bloom.

Monty goes South to explore gardens of early independent America and learns how the history of this part of the country is still very much evident in the places and people he meets. He visits the famous garden where President Thomas Jefferson, one of America's founding fathers, enjoyed spending his time seeking out seeds and plants for his thousand foot vegetable garden.

Monty explores the extraordinary scenery of the west coast of America. He begins his journey in Arizona where he learns about cacti and marvels at the sight of them in the desert and in private gardens where they have replaced traditional plants and lawns.

In the last programme of the current series, Monty Don takes stock of his year at Longmeadow. We visit RHS Wisley to learn why autumn leaves are such a precious commodity for our gardens, and in the final instalment of her botany series, Carol Klein celebrates the glorious displays put on by flowering plants to attract pollinators.

Monty Don has advice on how to successfully store an apple crop so it will last through winter and explains why he thinks it high time wall flowers came back into fashion. With tomatoes now over, Monty clears his greenhouse and plans for next year by planting garlic in the vegetable garden. Meanwhile, Carol is home at Glebe Cottage, dividing her perennials to continue the cost-effective stocking of her new beds.

Adam Frost is in his garden, catching viewers up on his new patio project and discussing his plans for the autumn. Arit Anderson travels to Somerset to meet landscape designer Dan Pearson, to find out about the design and planting principles he has used to create his own garden.

In the fourth of her films about botany, Carol Klein explores the inner workings of leaves - how they harness the sun's energy and turn it into food. Joe Swift meets Griff Rhys Jones for a private tour of his remarkable garden and discovers what a passionate gardener he is.
Monty Don prepares for his spring display and tackles slippery paths, Carol Klein visits a collection of Michaelmas daisies and we visit a veg grower with a show-stopping Halloween pumpkin.

Monty travels to two corners of the country where the challenges he faces are very different. On the south coast he is presented with a front garden ravaged by salty winds, and in Snowdonia he helps a mountainside garden.

Monty faces some of the most surprising plans yet - a Norwegian garden complete with waterfalls to be fashioned out of a tiny back yard in Dorset, and nothing less than a Japanese tea garden to be created out of a patch of ground in Bromley.

It is spring at Kew and after a long, dark winter, nature is coming back to life. Raymond makes his sublime version of rhubarb and custard and Kate finds out how a 12-year-old slave enabled vanilla to become the world's most popular flavour.

Summer has arrived at Kew and everything in Raymond Blanc and Kate Humble's garden is blooming. Butterflies and bees abound and there are new crops to tend, harvest and cook with. Everyone loves a carrot, particularly the carrot fly, so Raymond must protect his crop to ensure he has a good supply for his summer carrot stew.
Bobby, Christopher and John Ross work on J.R.'s masterpiece. J.R.'s will has lasting effects on the family legacy. Sue Ellen tries to get Gary (TED SHACKELFORD) out of Dallas.
Pamela's mother, Afton Cooper (AUDREY LANDERS), returns to Dallas. Emma is put in the middle of her father and grandmother's relationship, pushing her closer to Drew.
The Ewings' investigation of a conspiracy continuing to blame Christopher for recent events brings revelations in line with J.R.'s masterpiece. A new adversary is added to the mix.
After Cliff (KEN KERCHEVAL) and Ryland put Ewing Energies on the verge of collapse, the Ewings battle back. Christopher gets closer to finding his mother.
John Ross lets Pamela in on J.R.'s master plan, but his trust may be misplaced. Drew confides a dark secret to Elena, forcing her to choose between her family and Christopher.
John Ross and Pamela make a shocking discovery about an enemy's location the night J.R. was killed, compelling Bobby to reveal more of J.R.'s master plan. LEE MAJORS guest stars.
In the electrifying second season finale, the Ewings unite to execute J.R.'s master plan and the shocking answer to the question "Who killed J.R.?" is finally revealed.
The third season begins with the Ewings on top, having vanquished Cliff Barnes (KEN KERCHEVAL). But solidarity can only last for so long, and conflicts arise.
With Nicolas' arrival, John Ross tries to keep his plans moving forward, locking horns with Bobby in the process. Emma enlists the help of her grandmother (JUDITH LIGHT).
Bobby scrambles to outmaneuver John Ross' efforts to frack on Southfork. Christopher makes a startling discovery about Nicolas' past, as Nicolas and Elena's partnership heats up.
It's wedding day at Southfork and the groom, John Ross, has skipped out to strike a deal with a family adversary. AUDREY LANDERS, STEVE KANALY and CHARLENE TILTON) guest star.
Christopher learns surprising details about Heather's (ANNALYNNE McCORD) past and Cliff (KEN KERCHEVAL) persuades Elena to try a new tact. STEVEN WEBER appears as the Governor.
John Ross scrambles to keep the Arctic lease deal alive, even if he must betray those who love him most. Ryland's plot to keep Emma and John Ross apart takes an unexpected turn.
John Ross pushes ahead on his plans for control of Ewing Global, enlisting the help of one of J.R.'s last business partners. Elena's brother, Drew (KUNO BECKER), returns to Dallas.
Pamela's discovery that John Ross has been sleeping with Emma ignites a firestorm. As cliffhangers build, lives and relationships are brought to the brink.
The Ewing family searches for answers as to who set the fire at Southfork Ranch and who will survive. John Ross and Emma struggle with their role in Pamela's overdose.
Christopher and Heather's (ANNALYNNE McCORD) relationship is tested as John Ross tries to redeem himself with Pamela. Elena makes a drastic move to get justice for her family.
Elena finally confronts the Ewings. The family is shocked, realigning relationships and forcing Bobby to re-examine the steps he took to implement J.R.'s master plan.
As Ewing Global goes public, everyone scrambles to claim ownership. Bobby seeks the aide of old flame (MELINDA CLARKE) to help get back control of the company.
Elena learns the truth about Nicolass connections to the cartel, which sends her spiraling and Christopher fears for her safety. Bobby must make a choice he never anticipated.
Nicolas tries to prove himself to Elena by making a deal with the authorities that puts him on a collision course with John Ross' plan and places both their lives in jeopardy.
In the season finale, enemies are unmasked, new alliances are formed and John Ross learns a shocking secret about J.R. that sends him in search of a surprising new cohort.

In the early 1980s, the decapitation of a young African-American male led the Miami-Dade police department and the FBI along a trail of murder.  Investigators quickly discovered that the victim was a dissident member of a religious sect headed by a man calling himself Yahweh ben Yahweh, or God, Son of God.  Although the FBI believed Yahweh ben Yahweh and his followers were responsible for many murders, they could find no direct evidence linking them to the crimes.

In November of 1994, when a Wells Fargo armored van disappeared from a Glendale, Arizona mall, local authorities and the FBI scrambled to recover it, and its cargo of nearly a million dollars. Six hours later, agents found the van, its driver shot dead inside and the money gone. It was a perfect hit by professionals who left no clue behind. Months passed before a solid lead developed. In January, a tip led agents to look into a former prison guard.

Beginning in California in 1995, a serial killer targeted vulnerable women. At first charming and generous, he quickly became violent. He was brutal with his kills and quick in his getaways. Traveling across the country, he struck in Mississippi, Louisiana and Florida. The FBI and local police needed to stop this cross-country killer before more women fell victim to his insatiable rage.

In 1987, a successful television producer was gunned down in his New York office.  It looked like a professional hit.  With no leads, the investigation stalled.  Four years later and a continent away, a man told Los Angeles police he had been hired to murder two exotic dancers.  Investigators linked the two crimes and uncovered a businessman willing to kill to protect his interests.

A 1981 armored car robbery near New York City left one guard dead and another critically wounded.  Police stopped suspects nearby and another shoot-out ensued, claiming the lives of two officers.  Local police and the FBI suspected a large group of domestic terrorists with a history of violent crime.  They would try to ferret out these heavily armed criminals who moved in a shadowy underworld and were not afraid to kill authorities.

When a California man was found dismembered in 1990, police suspected a local burglar, but they couldn't find him.  Six months later, he was caught robbing an Arizona bank and sentenced to life.  But prison couldn't hold him for long, and within a year he escaped.  The FBI would lead a multi-agency manhunt for a killer on a desperate run through the tourist regions of the west.

At first it seemed like a tragic hunting accident when 18-year-old David Wilkey was shot to death in rural Virginia in 1983.  A tenacious insurance investigator suspected foul play, but he had no direct evidence. Two years later a man contacted North Carolina FBI agents with a complex story of conspiracy and murder-for-hire: he claimed he had been hired to murder Wilkey's killer.

On a summer night in 1990, a body was discovered burning in a Minnesota alley.  Weeks later, police finally identified the victim, a suspected drug courier from California.  The FBI began working with local police and slowly uncovered a multi-state crime ring run by a deadly drug lord who used violence and intimidation to keep those around him silent.  Agents needed to infiltrate and dismantle the crew before more people died.

In the early 1990's drug gangs terrorized Harlem, New York neighborhoods. When a 10-year-old boy fell victim in the crossfire, NYPD detectives and FBI agents clamped down on the problem. They formed a task force called C-11, designed to dismantle the gangs. In an environment of violence and fear it would be difficult to identify, arrest and convict those involved in the secretive and deadly world of big money drugs.

In 1994, a teenage immigrant came to the United States to realize her dream of becoming a doctor.  But a tragic twist of fate intervened, when she found herself an innocent victim of the drug trade.  Kidnapped and held captive, she survived for days against all odds.  Authorities arrested her captors, but they refused to reveal her whereabouts. The FBI and local police raced against time, determined to save the teenager's life. Their investigation revealed a complex story of drugs, betrayal and

In the mid-1990's, a gang of professional bank robbers raided cities across seven states. Disguises and speed protected their identity from cameras and the police as they stole hundreds of thousands of dollars, always leaving a bomb to terrorize their victims. The stakes were raised when the FBI discovered the robbers had an agenda beyond their personal wealth. To stop these extremists and their growing operation, the FBI needed to capture their leaders.

A Labor Day weekend turned into a nightmare of murder as a cross-country crime spree terrorized the nation.  In a small Ohio community, an elderly woman and a teenage boy disappeared within hours of each other.  Police believed the cases were linked, but didn't know how. They contacted the FBI for help.  A trail of stolen vehicles and murder victims across seven states led agents on a hunt for two suspected killers. Their only hope of stopping them was to anticipate the killers' next move.

A day that began with a class field trip ended with a parent's worst nightmare.  An 11-year-old girl was missing.  Her parents were certain she was no runaway.  When they failed to find her in their quiet Illinois neighborhood, they called the police.  The FBI soon joined the investigation and family and friends worked with detectives and agents in an urgent search for the missing girl.  Faced with conflicting witness reports and false leads, agents wouldn't stop until they found the girl, and t

In the summer of 1988, a wealthy Jackson, Mississippi woman disappeared from her home in broad daylight.  Left behind was a mysterious ransom note listing twelve names and no specific instructions.  The note, and a few drops of blood were the only clues to her fate. FBI and local police struggled to find answers in the cryptic message so they could find the kidnapper and retrieve the victim before her time ran out. Solving the crime required the keen insight of a criminal profiler and the persev

In Arizona, a shipment of money vanished into the high desert, along with the two men hired to guard it.  The FBI didn't know if the guards were participants or victims of an ambush.  Answers lay somewhere in the thousands of square miles of Arizona's northwest territory.  When the vehicle was recovered with three hundred thousand dollars and the drivers missing, suspicions that the crime was an inside job grew.

In Alabama, a pair of convicted felons escaped the custody of a local deputy and fled across the country.  Eluding authorities, they moved from state to state in a wave of abduction and car theft.  When a foreign military officer disappeared along their trail, police and FBI agents wondered if the armed fugitives had become killers.  Agents believed the pair were growing more violent and raced to find the escapees before more victims crossed their path.

In 1992, a young mother was gunned down in front of her children.  Police searched for answers, but found none. The horrible crime appeared unmotivated, senseless, and random. Then, family members offered a startling clue.  The victim, the wife of a prominent Atlanta attorney, was also a woman burdened with a secret; a secret the FBI believed led to her death.  It would force local and federal agents to untangle an intricate web of money, drugs and murder.

In Memphis, Tennessee, a horrible crime terrified local residents.  When a wealthy young mother was abducted in front of her in-laws' home, the police had no shortage of suspects.  The twenty-five year old victim left behind a tumultuous marriage, an ex-husband, and several spurned boyfriends.  All were on the FBI's short list.  To find the woman and her abductor, investigators would have to first determine the motive.

In 1997, a series of crimes in a small Iowa farming community left residents reeling in shock and fear. Two young men went on a crime spree of robbery, kidnapping and murder, and then disappeared. By the time they were identified, they already had a twelve-hour lead. As the hunt for the two men expanded, the FBI committed its resources to tracking down the suspects. The pursuit would take agents across six states to catch the killers before they struck again.

In the late 80's, Florida's cocaine imports were among the highest in the nation.  Regional territories were enforced with intimidation and murder.  Desperate to stop the violence, local authorities turned to the FBI for help. One dealer bowed to no one.  He would stop at nothing to keep detectives and agents from building a case against him.  When his organization began targeting the government itself, a city went on high alert.

In Kokomo, Indiana an unthinkable crime terrified residents. A young woman was snatched from her home on a bright spring morning.  Drops of blood and a torn window screen were all that was left to tell authorities what happened to the twenty-one year old victim. After several days of searching, a former FBI profiler narrowed the suspect list to one. Agents and detectives followed the trail across state lines hoping to find the victim before her time ran out.

In July 1997, a triple murder terrified residents in the nation's capital. In a Georgetown coffee shop, three employees were shot to death. Investigators could find no immediate suspects and no clear motive for the attack. Evidence at the crime scene pointed in many different directions. Was this a hate crime, a robbery gone wrong, or an act of cold-blooded vengeance against one of the victims?

In 1986, a small crime free Indiana town was turned inside out by the arrival of one dangerous stranger. After an officer was gunned down at point-blank range, the psychotic killer led investigators across the Midwest. No one knew where the gunman would strike next, even as his tally of murders and abductions grew. The FBI and state police raced against time to rescue America's heartland from this deranged gunman, before he killed again.

In Langley, Virginia, a gunman fired into rush hour traffic.  The brazen daytime shooting of employees from the Central Intelligence Agency stunned the country.  The victims seemed randomly selected, but the motive appeared to be political. The FBI was called in, but the nationwide search quickly became a far-reaching international manhunt. Agents processed more than 2000 leads and crossed an ocean in the effort to deliver justice.

On the day before Thanksgiving, a mother discovered her 10 year-old son was missing from his school. No one knew how it could have happened.  Within hours, the boy's entire family was frantically searching for him. The few leads in the case quickly turned cold and the FBI was called in to aid in the investigation. The search by agents and local authorities would cover a thousand miles to expose the kidnapper and find the missing child.

On a summer afternoon in upscale Lodi, California, a 12-year-old girl is abducted from her home.  Scores of police officers and FBI agents converge, determined to find the young girl before it is too late.  When the kidnapper's car is discovered in a field near Lodi, police dogs, helicopters, and hundreds of volunteers are employed in a round-the-clock search.  It would take a community united in concern for one of their youngest to find the missing child.

In rural Texas, 13-year-old is kidnapped on her way to school.  Frantic to find her safely, her millionaire father calls local authorities and the FBI.  As police officers and agents conduct aerial surveillance, the father drives hundreds of miles through the night to deliver the ransom cash to a drop that the kidnappers keep changing.  In a final effort to save the young girl, investigators must engage in a dangerous firefight with five desperate criminals.

In September 1997, a team of masked gunmen robbed an armored car facility in Los Angeles, and made off with $18.9 million, the largest takeover heist in U.S. history.  An employee believed she recognized the voice of one of the robbers, and FBI agents began conducting surveillance on a former employee of the facility.  With only one piece of physical evidence, a fragment of a vehicle taillight, authorities hoped to connect him to the crime, and locate his accomplices.

In July 1996, two men entered a pawnshop in Birmingham, Alabama, and ruthlessly murdered the employees.  Unbeknownst to the killers, a secret video surveillance camera recorded the shooting.  Local police and the FBI released images of the crime to the media, and were quickly able to identify the perpetrators.  Now authorities had to find two cold-blooded killers who knew that they were being pursued for murder one.

In Lincoln County, Nebraska, a fugitive drug dealer engaged in a shootout with state troopers, wounding two of them, and eluded capture after a high-speed chase.  Authorities immediately set up a statewide manhunt, connecting the fugitive to a murder in western Nebraska.  A chance sighting led FBI agents to a second confrontation with the killer, who was more determined than ever to escape the law.

After a career criminal committed a vehicular homicide in New Orleans, FBI agents tracked him through his habits and addictions.  They focused their investigation on gambling communities throughout the country and, when he resurfaced in Atlantic City, authorities used all of their resources to trap an elusive sociopath who claimed that he would never be taken alive.

In the early 1980's, a pair of serial bank robbers gained a reputation among law enforcement officials as formidable bandits.  Using the same modus operandi, the two men took hostages and emptied bank vaults across the Midwest.  After the criminals escaped from police custody, FBI agents familiar with the bandits believed that they would attempt a grand-scale heist.  By conducting surveillance on known associates of the criminals, authorities tried to anticipate the next target.

In the summer of 1999, Texas was terrorized by a brutal serial killer who traveled by train.  The FBI assembled a task force to gather information about the dangerous drifter and create a profile that would help locate him.  As they learned that the killer had traveled extensively through the United States and Mexico, the murders became more frequent, and authorities had to cast a dragnet over an entire continent in an effort to catch him.

On October 2, 1987, a Boston police officer responding to a domestic disturbance call was fatally wounded.  Local authorities launched a citywide manhunt, but were only able to find the fingerprints of the chief suspect.  Believing that he had fled the area, the FBI followed the suspect's trail to the west coast and then across the Mexican border, always aware of the desperation of a cop killer and of the need for justice.

In August 1984, the son of a successful real estate developer was kidnapped in front of his father's business in Miami.  After the father received a $3 million ransom demand from a self-proclaimed terrorist, the FBI became involved.  Based on witness descriptions of the car used in the kidnapping, authorities began to suspect a pair of Colombian nationals with a known grudge against the developer's family.

In October 1995, a South Carolina family was taken hostage as part of an elaborately planned bank robbery.  Local police quickly identified two of the perpetrators, but the criminal mastermind proved more elusive.  After his escape from custody, authorities began to suspect the fugitive of involvement in a series of bank robberies up and down the east coast, and the FBI remained on his trail, hoping to catch him before he took more hostages.

In February 1988, a record store clerk in Sandusky, Ohio, was fatally shot in his van.  After discovering a night deposit bag with thousands of dollars in the vehicle, police knew that robbery was not the motive, and began to investigate other possibilities.  FBI agents learned that several motorcycle gang members had been stopped nearby on a traffic violation shortly after the murder and theorized that the clerk's murder may have been a botched hit carried out by a gang member.

In June 1973, a young girl was abducted from a state park on the Missouri River while camping with her family.  Several months passed with no leads, then an FBI agent took a particular interest in the case.  Using a new technique known as criminal profiling, he predicted that the kidnapper would contact the girl's family on the one-year anniversary of her abduction.  When this prediction came true, the FBI agent noted behavioral clues, hoping that they could lead him to the kidnapper.

In 1996, a group of political extremists twice robbed a bank in Spokane, Washington, using homemade bombs and military precision to escape.   The FBI learned that the robbers, part of a shadowy organization called the Phineas Priesthood, might be preparing for a small-scale war with law enforcement.  After the suspects were identified, the FBI was faced with the task of safely arresting a group of terrorists with a deadly agenda.

In August 1992, a man returned to his Memphis home and discovered that his wife was missing.  The husband, as well as his friends, family and neighbors began to receive ransom calls.  FBI agents noticed that one neighbor seemed to have the best rapport with the kidnapper.  They began to question his level of involvement, but had to proceed carefully, knowing that he could be their only link to the missing woman.

In 1990 and 1991, Chicago police and the FBI were on the trail of a bank robber whose holdups were becoming increasingly violent.  The criminal consistently used stolen Japanese cars to carry out the robberies, so authorities hoped to identify him by tracking vehicle thefts.  When they finally located the man known as the bearded bandit, they learned that he did not work alone and he had made a pact never to surrender.

In 1988, new light was shed on the mysterious death of a South Carolina farmer when a criminal confessed that two prominent community members hired him to commit murder.  Local police and FBI agents arrested a wealthy businessman and later learned that, even behind bars, he commanded the power to corrupt and kill.  Using prison informants, agents had to prevent him from murdering again.

programmes.d: In Seoul, a soon after acquiring independence from Japanese occupation, two men met and there came the sound of six shots firing. After this meeting, Inuyashiki studies his abilities, and uses them to save others. Meanwhile, Shishigami confronts a group of delinquents who have been tormenting his best friend Naoyuki Ando.

When the fully tattooed yakuza criminal Samejima finds a girl he likes, he kidnaps them, drugs them up, and then roughs them up. Fumino was happy. She had a job and a fiance. But one night, Samejima sets his sights on her, and has his men kidnap her. Fumino manages to escape, and runs to her fiance Satoru's house, but Samejima is in hot pursuit. Inuyashiki comes to save them, but gets shot.

Ando is struggling with the fact that his friend Shishigami is responsible for the spree of home invasions. After reading that hospital patients were being cured, Ando theorizes that there is someone else out there with the same powers as Shishigami. Ando lures Inuyashiki by pretending to need help and asks him to stop Shishigami. Meanwhile, Shishigami learns his mother has terminal cancer.

When a princess with a priceless jewel comes to town, Inspector Nakamori is sidelined by a detective from her country who shoots first and... shoots again later, until his quarry is killed. Naturally, his target is Kid the Phantom Thief!

Kid the Phantom Thief literally rises to the occasion when old man Jirokichi of the Suzuki conglomerate throws down the gauntlet. But with Detective Conan as part of the security team guarding the Blue Wonder jewel, will Kaito finally get his wings clipped?

Kid's next target is Green Dream, the world's largest emerald and a one-time-only stage prop for a local play. Though the venue is crawling with cops under Nakamori's command, will Kid be able to make off with Green Dream as well as make a young actress's dream come true?

Ed uncovers a conspiracy of staggering scope: a plot that has already claimed countless victims. Clues suggest that Fort Briggs will soon know bloodshed - and an entire nation will suffer.

As Raven tries to corrupt Armstrong, Ed and Al can only wait in their cell. Long ago, their father faced his own captivity, confined to an eternity of regret in an undying body. To escape the pain, he said goodbye.

Rouge, aboard Crimson Egg, makes a discovery of a secret room that carries a strange capsule powered by a Chaos Emerald. Much to her surprise she discovers that Shadow is hibernating inside.
As Shadow tries to recall who Sonic and his friends when a Metarex named Scarship arrives to complete its newly assigned mission: to destroy Sonic and Dr. Eggman.

Orion's Crown has been stolen and is up for grabs at a black-market auction. Lupin has his eyes on both the crown and the auction money, but first he must outsmart the other parties vying for the crown, including Fujiko. Furthermore, Jigen is working for the seller and Goemon is working for a bidder. With an auction full of deceit and trickery, who will ultimately get the crown?

A two-thousand-year-old casket has been excavated. Inside the casket is Camilla, a beautiful woman in a near-death state, holding a golden statuette of the Virgin Mary. Lupin attempts to steal the golden statuette, but things don't go as planned when Camilla, a vampire awakes from her long slumber. Will Lupin be able to save Fujiko from being sacrificed for Camilla's revenge?

It's a New Year's special where the entire cast of Beelzebub acts out everyone's favorite ancient Chinese fable, Journey to the West! See the gang as Son Goku, Sanzou the monk, and everyone else in their quest to reach Tenjiku and obtain the sacred sutra! Or maybe just to eat takoyaki! Whatever!
It's time to start the Pudding-Pudding Exercises!

As Raven tries to corrupt Armstrong, Ed and Al can only wait in their cell. Long ago, their father faced his own captivity, confined to an eternity of regret in an undying body. To escape the pain, he said goodbye.
